owned_invariants: The host reads the checker, the public input, the seed, the workflow id and the checked answer from a turn's task.json and receipt.json itself. The caller supplies the two files and a name for the run, and cannot supply a verdict, a class, an id or a count.
A full-slot answer is judged on its task_result and gives its DDC letters in order; any other answer is judged as written. An object whose DDC moves cannot be read is refused as BAD_TURN.

A failure record is written only for a turn whose task result the judge rejects. A turn without a checked answer is refused as NO_ANSWER, a correct one as NOT_A_FAILURE, a turn with no judge as UNKNOWN_CHECKER.

A case is named c plus 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of a domain tag, the checker and the case's integers in order, so the name does not depend on how the input was written, on the task id or on the run. A failure id is the case name, an @ and the run name.
The failure's evidence hash covers the checker, the public input and the whole stored answer.

A trial pair counts only when both turns are the same case, the baseline seed is the base seed with the rules admitted at the stated ledger head, and the treated seed is that plus the rule under trial. Anything else is refused as PAIR_MISMATCH, BASELINE_SEED_MISMATCH or TREATED_SEED_MISMATCH.
In a trial a turn without a checked answer is not correct. Held-out ids are the case names, so the ledger refuses a trial on the case of a failure the rule came from.
boundaries: The host trusts the two stored files. The workflow's own replay is what ties a receipt to the reply bytes and a task to the prompt that was sent.
One judge exists: integer_sum_v1. A mining turn has no judge and is never a failure or a trial case.
Two cases with the same integers in another order are different cases.
A case name is 64 bits of a hash; equal names are treated as the same case.
